AgentCommand.description: A command an agent ran with its shell tool (Claude Code's Bash, Droid's Execute), as its hooks tell it (`kelp hook command`): what it ran, how that went and the end of what it printed. The session's tab lists them (`session.commands`), its row shows the one running.

description.description: The agent's own words for it ("Run the tests").

output.description: The last `outputLimit` bytes it printed (stdout, then stderr).

AgentSessionInfo.description: One resumable conversation of a CLI coding agent, read from its on-disk transcript (AgentData reads them).

messageCount.description: Exact for small files; extrapolated from the head and tail for large ones.

id.description: nil: not found, or it printed no version (`latest`: not on npm, or npm isn't installed).

ahead.description: Commits to push: past the upstream, or with none, on no remote branch (what the graph marks "not pushed yet").

CIRuns.Failure.description: One thing that broke: a test, or a compiler's error (no `test`), with where and what, read from a job's log.

file.description: Relative to the project where the log says enough to tell.

CIRuns.Report.description: What a failed log says. `failures` comes from the whole log, before `log` keeps only its tail.

exitCode.description: For a log in no known format: how it ended, and the lines before that.

more.description: Failures left out past the cap.

tests.description: Tests that ran, when the log counts them.

CIRuns.Workflow.description: A workflow you can start by hand (`on: workflow_dispatch`), with the inputs its form asks for.

ChangedEvent.description: Projects or workspaces changed: read the lists again. The params are just the word. Still sent for clients that read lists; the changed records themselves come as `event.repo` / `event.worktree` / `event.removed`.

CloneEvent.description: A line of `git clone`'s progress, to the connection that started the clone.

CodeCompletion.description: One completion: what the list shows and what goes in.

CodeProblem.description: An error or warning a language server found: from `line`, `column` to `endLine`, `endColumn`, all 0-based, in UTF-16 units.

CodeSymbol.description: A name a file defines: what it's called, what it is ("class", "function"…) and its 1-based line.

CommitDetails.description: A commit's message body (the subject is the graph's), its author's email, and its size against the first parent.

ContextEvent.description: Nil usage: not known (not Claude Code, ended, just compacted).

Delivered.description: How many Kelp windows were told.

DevServerEvent.description: A dev server in a workspace printed its local URL.

noNewline.description: The file's last line, with no newline after it (git's "\ No newline at end of file").

category.description: What the library files it under: tools, themes, icons, languages, agents or integrations. nil: an index from before categories.

requires.description: Commands it needs on PATH (an extension without them stays inactive).

source.description: The reviewed folder on GitHub, at its commit: what `extension.fetch` takes.

header.description: Raw `diff --git` / `---` / `+++` lines, needed to rebuild patches for hunk staging.

latin1.description: The file isn't UTF-8: its text was read byte for byte (Latin-1), and patches go back the same way.

tooLarge.description: Its changes are past what one reply carries (`Git.diffBudget`): no hunks, only the header. Asked for alone, it may fit.

FileEvent.description: A watched file's version now: the stamp `files.read` and `files.write` give (nil: it's gone, or isn't a file). Only the stamp: whoever holds that version (the app's own save) has nothing to read. A touch is a new version too. `problems`: what its language server says is wrong with it, pushed as the server says it.

FilesEvent.description: A watched workspace's files as `files.list` gives them, and what git ignores (`files.ignored`), pushed when that changed. `error`: they couldn't be listed.

stamp.description: What's there now; its text nil when that isn't UTF-8.

GitEvent.description: A watched workspace's git, read again after its files changed. `error`: git couldn't say (not a repository…).

name.description: `bucket` is gh's category of `state`: pass, fail, pending, skipping, cancel.

title.description: `type` is Issue, PullRequest or DraftIssue; drafts have no url.

path.description: path/line are nil for top-level review bodies.

GitWebPages.Pages.description: `forge`: "github" | "gitlab" | "bitbucket"; `ci`: Actions / Pipelines; `pulls`: pull or merge requests.

GraphCommit.description: One row of the commit graph (VS Code's Source Control Graph). Lines are lane pairs: `top` runs from the row's top edge (lane `[0]`) to its middle (lane `[1]`), `bottom` from the middle to the bottom edge.

LimitHit.description: A plan limit that stopped a session's turn.

at.description: When it stopped: `resets` is read from here, so "3pm" stays today's once that has passed.

resets.description: When it resets, as the agent printed it ("3:40pm", "Oct 20 at 5am"); nil when it didn't say.

LineStats.description: Lines added / removed in the working tree (staged, unstaged and new files) against HEAD, split by what kind of file.

LinearState.description: `type` is Linear's state category: triage, backlog, unstarted, started, completed, canceled.

OutputEvent.description: What a session printed, to a client attached with JSON (`session.attach`), not as a byte pipe.

PortBusyEvent.description: A run couldn't start: what it printed says `port` is taken.

PortsList.Port.description: A port a process of one of the workspace's sessions listens on; on a remote project's host, one in its folder.

host.description: On a remote project: its host, the port on this Mac once forwarded, and true when the host can't be asked (this is its last answer).

port.description: `session`: "" when it can't be told. `pid` 0: none, a forwarding asked for by hand.

RemovedEvent.description: A project, workspace or session record that's gone (a project takes its workspaces with it; their sessions each say so).

copyFiles.description: Glob-ish file names copied from the repo into each new worktree (e.g. ".env").

removable.description: Nothing uncommitted or untracked, not locked, not one of Kelp's workspaces (those go with Delete Workspace).

Routine.description: An agent on a schedule: at its time the daemon starts `agent` with `prompt` in the routine's own workspace (a desk in the project's folder, made at its first run), and keeps how each run went.

checked.description: Due times up to here are handled: run, missed, or before the routine was on.

id.description: Empty: a new one (routine.set gives it an id).

onWake.description: A run missed while the Mac slept or Kelp wasn't running: once when it's back (true), or skipped.

time.description: Minutes after midnight; hourly: minutes past the hour.

weekday.description: Weekly: 1 Sunday … 7 Saturday, as Calendar counts.

Routine.Run.description: One run: its agent's session, and how it went.

due.description: When it was due; Run Now: when it was asked for.

summary.description: The agent's first line when done, what it asks, why it failed.

RoutinesEvent.description: Every routine and their runs of the last two weeks, newest run first: routine.list's answer, and `event.routines`, sent whenever one of them changes.

RunOption.description: Something the project's own files say can be run: a package.json script, a Makefile target, a compose service, a Python app… (`run.detect`). It runs only when someone picks it (`run.start`), never because a project was opened.

detail.description: What the entry says, when that isn't the command (a script's body, a service's port).

folder.description: Where it runs, inside the workspace ("" is its own folder).

id.description: "folder|file|name": the same while the file keeps the entry, so a choice can be remembered.

missing.description: The program it needs that isn't on that machine's PATH.

digest.description: Of exactly the text read: `scripts.trust` trusts what was shown, not a later version.

argv.description: Launch options, kept so "Restart" reproduces the session.

awaiting.description: The one of them it waits for (a test run, not a server): its tab glows for it while it works. A Stop says which; one sent to the background mid-turn counts until then, unless it looks like a server. nil when it waits for none.

background.description: Commands it started in the background that still ran when its turn ended (a test run it waits for, a dev server).

continueAt.description: When Kelp types "continue" into it, if it still stands where the limit left it (`session.continueAt`).

exitCode.description: How its program ended: the exit code, or 128 + the signal that stopped it; nil while it runs.

goal.description: The /goal it works toward (Claude Code checks it after each turn and goes on until it's met); nil without one.

limitHit.description: The plan limit that stopped it; nil again once it does anything else.

parent.description: The agent that started it (`kelp session new --agent`): it hears how this one is doing and takes it along when it ends.

profile.description: The account profile it started with (Settings › Accounts); nil: the agent's own default login. Kept so a woken or restarted session comes back on the same account.

progress.description: How far what runs in it got, 0–100, when it says (OSC 7501's `progress`, `kelp report`, ConEmu's OSC 9;4).

running.description: The command its shell tool runs now (`AgentCommand`, from its hooks); nil between them.

startedBy.description: The agent a command belongs to (`kelp session new --cmd` inside it): the line under that agent's terminal shows it, instead of a tab and a sidebar row of its own. Unlike a child, it goes on when the agent ends, and gets a tab then.

statusAt.description: When `status` last changed ("working for 4m", "done 2h ago"); nil for sessions from before it was kept.

subagentRuns.description: Its subagents of this turn in the order they started, the finished ones too; follows the two above, ends with the turn.

subagentTasks.description: What each of them does, by the same id, when the agent says (OSC 7501's `title`).

subagents.description: Its own subagents at work now, by id, and what kind each is (its hooks say): they run inside it, with no tab of their own.

summary.description: One-line summary of what the agent did / is asking (local model or hooks).

title.description: Tab title (from the first prompt, or set by hand — a manual name wins).

tmux.description: The tmux session on a remote project's host its agent runs in (`RemoteHost.command(_:inTmux:)`), so the agent outlives a dropped connection and the daemon; kept so a wake or a restart attaches to it again. nil elsewhere, and once Kelp ended that tmux session (Stop, closing the tab).

workDir.description: Where the agent works when it left `cwd` (Claude Code going into its `.claude/worktrees/…`), from its hooks; nil while it works in `cwd`. Paths it prints and its last turn's changes are read there; a restart still starts in `cwd`.

top.description: The biggest three, biggest first; `more` items besides them.

base.description: In Kind's order, the empty ones left out.

setup.description: The base as the agent itself splits it, when it says (Claude Code's /context).

SessionContextParts.Setup.description: What every request starts with, as Claude Code's /context counts it: system prompt, tools, MCP, memory files, skills… (`parts`, in its order, summing to the base), with the biggest items of some ("CLAUDE.md 4k").

buffer.description: Kept free for compacting: the conversation compacts by itself before it reaches this.

deferred.description: Tools it loads only when one is used ("MCP tools (deferred)"): not in the context.

label.description: As Claude Code names it: "System prompt", "Memory files".

cacheUntil.description: When the prompt cache goes cold, by what the last reply wrote to it; nil when that isn't known.

touched.description: When its transcript last changed: a long quiet is a long command, or a subagent that hangs.

SessionTurn.Turn.description: One turn of the agent: what it changed by the time it stopped, and how long it worked.

SessionUsage.Usage.description: CPU (ps's %, summed over the session's processes; 100 = one core) and resident memory of a live session.

SettingsEvent.description: settings.json changed (a set, or the file edited by hand): all of it now.

Subagent.description: A subagent of an agent's turn, at work or finished. `kind` is empty when only a terminal report told of it.

SubagentStep.description: One thing a subagent did: the tool, and the path or command it was given.

setupNeedsTrust.description: The project's .kelp.yaml has a setup that didn't run: it isn't trusted yet.

activity.description: When someone last typed in it or it printed something.

UIEvent.description: An agent's `ui.open` / `ui.command`, relayed to the app: the request's fields and which it was.

Unsynced.description: The newest commits a sync would move: `outgoing` is what a push sends, `incoming` what a pull brings (none without an upstream).

UsageAgents.Agent.description: One agent over the span: its tokens by kind (`input` leaves the cache out) and its own models and projects.

days.description: `days` by day ("yyyy-MM-dd") and agent id; agents and groups most expensive first; `since` is the first day's start.

UsageGet.Block.description: Tokens and their API price over a span (dates as seconds since 1970).

block.description: The 5-hour block now, if one is running.

UsageGet.Codex.description: Codex's own limits from its latest log line (percent used, resets as seconds since 1970).

UsageGet.Limit.description: One limit as an agent shows it: kind ("session", "week", "week · Fable"…), percent used, when it resets.

observedAt.description: When a session printed it (Claude's percentages from the last 12 hours); nil for a /usage reading.

plans.description: By agent id: the latest /usage readings, and when they were read.

days.description: Most expensive first; `since` is the first day's start (seconds since 1970).

WatchTopic.description: What can be watched, and what its key names.

base.description: Branch this one was cut from; when it isn't the repo's base the worktree is part of a PR stack.

issue.description: Links to the task it came from and the PR it became: "#123" / "ENG-123".

WorktreeCreate.Result.description: The worktree's own fields, and beside them what its .kelp.yaml setup needs.

info.description: JSON-RPC 2.0, one message a line, over the Unix socket at ~/.kelp/kelp.sock. A method marked x-internal is for Kelp's own window and tools: it gets no promise. Events are notifications: x-events lists them, and sets up none of them.
info.title: Kelp daemon

methods.description: A file with `text` (empty by default), or a folder, with the folders above it → its path. `unique`: when the name is taken, the first free one of "name 2.ext", "name 3.ext"… (Finder's "untitled 2"); otherwise a taken name fails.

methods.description: A remote project's file copied to this Mac for a viewer that reads a file (an image, a PDF, what Quick Look shows) → the copy's path; a file here → its own path. Refused like `files.read` (a pipe, past the size limit), text or not.

methods.description: The file's text and its stamp. Fails with an `Unopenable` error where a tab would refuse it (a pipe, past the size limit, not UTF-8), or saying it was moved or deleted.

methods.description: Writes `text` (UTF-8, atomically, through a symlink to the file it points at) when the file is still `base`, the stamp it was read or last written as; with no `base`, whatever is there (Save Here, Keep Mine, a new file). → {stamp}: written. → {conflict}: unwritten, it changed since (an agent's edit). → {missing: true}: unwritten, it's gone.
methods.name: files.write

methods.description: Writes `text` to that file on the host → null; → {changed: its text there} instead, unwritten, when it's no longer `base` (an agent there edited it since it was read).
